events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Ambushed General

options.text: This is his own fault. [character], bring me back my army!
No one can be trusted.
Warn the [rival] of untold horrors if they do not return [character].

events.text: With his forces dwindling, [character] made a deal with a local guide to lead his troops around the enemy. It was a trap. Beset on all sides, the last of [character]’s forces quickly crumbled. Now a messenger has arrived from [rival], informing us that along with the slaughter of his troops, [character] has been captured and is to be held indefinitely.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Bitter Rivals

options.text: Bring more generals to the field.
Focus on treating [character].
Promise to have vengeance against [rival].

events.text: Over time, the fighting with [rival] has grown ever more vicious as your troops hear rumors about the atrocities of the other side and seek to take revenge, or just escape such a fate themselves. With another unit lost in the recent fighting and [character] wounded, your people have turned the general into a symbol of national pride. They are angrier than ever and look to you to take action against [rival].

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Bleeding for [rival]

options.text: Talk to the officers. Move the [family] away from the action.
I am not on the throne to play favorites.
We will work harder to to prevent such loss in one family.

events.text: More deaths on the battlefield. More blood shed for [rival]. You find your Chancellor alone in the throne chamber, hanging his weary head. "Those men," he murmurs. "So many of them [family] boys." With a haunted look, [character] beseeches you. "Reassign my family's units away from the fighting. Please. We will forever be in your debt. Let others bleed for [rival]."

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: By His own Sword

options.text: He should have lived to make amends.
It was a noble end.

events.text: Seeing the defeat of his forces, [character] decided to fall upon his own sword rather than returning to [rival] in disgrace. Upon hearing the news, [character] and [character] strike up a debate on the nature of a good death. [character] suggests that it was a noble act, while [character] claims that [character] would have served [rival] better by living to fight another day. Will you side with [character] or [character]?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Call to Action

options.text: Allocate more gold for our war efforts.
We cannot afford more funds.
I will find other ways to support our troops.

events.text: After the rout of our troops by [rival] forces, General [character] sends the court a scathing message. Frustrated at the military leadership's mistakes, he demands more resources for the soldiers at the front. It is a matter of life and death. How shall we respond?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Captured General

options.text: We will pay the ransom.
We do not bend to demands.

events.text: Your general [character] has been captured in combat! Your enemy is demanding a ransom for his safe return. How shall we respond?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Captured and Wounded

options.text: We will try to gather the ransom money.

events.text: Your general [character] was wounded in the thick of the recent fighting. Stuck in the leg while on horseback, he was quickly pulled down and taken prisoner as the rest of his forces were routed. [character] may be lost for now, but there is still hope of returning him to [rival].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Cease Fire Tragedy

options.text: [character] was a fool for trusting them.
There would have been no fight if the boy remained calm.
Remember our true enemy, the [rival] killed them both.

events.text: A lone soldier returns from the recent fighting, battered and bloody. The haunted look in his eyes speaks of tragedy before his mouth even opens. After days of fighting, the troops under [character]’s command were at breaking point. Finally [character] agreed to meet with the [rival] leader, taking a small cohort of officers and guards into the enemy camp. They never had a chance to talk. A young [family] officer-in-training, spooked by the idea of a trap, grabbed the bridle of [character]’s horse in a sudden movement. The ensuing massacre was swift and violent, with only one soldier left alive to tell the tale. Upon hearing the news the devastated [family] blame the [family] boy for the death of [character]. How will you intervene?

events.author: Solver
events.name: Desertion

options.text: Perhaps we will be better off without him.

events.text: After a major defeat, survivors bring you more bad news. As soon as the tide of the battle turned against our forces, [character] abandoned the battlefield, leaving the soldiers to fend for themselves.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Family of the Dead

options.text: A grand festival in his name.
Inscriptions commemorating his heroic deeds.
The time and resources are best used elsewhere.

events.text: Your General [character] has fallen in battle,. His family, the [family] family, ask for you to honor him in their Family Seat of [city]. How will you honor the dead?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Flee the Field

options.text: Flee the field.
Go down with your men.

events.text: The battlefield is a slaughterhouse. Your bodyguard lay strew around you and suddenly you realize just how alone you are. Only a handful of men stand with you, mostly lesser members of the nation’s head families. Soldiers are starting to encircle you but it’s impossible to make out if they’re friend or foe from the blood and sweat running into your eyes. “The battle is lost! Please, you must escape.” The soldier’s outstretched hand offers a horse’s bridle. The encircling troops are closing in. It’s now or never.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Hero Stone

options.text: [character] deserves the grandest of stones.
Get poets to recite tales of his prowess by the stone.
Make a speech about his bravery.

events.text: [character] has fallen, the latest warrior to die protecting [rival], and the [family] have decided to honor him with a hero stone. For [character], they want to carve the largest known, a towering stone with five different panels of intricate carvings of the heavens, [character] ascending, and scenes of battle. To fully realize their ambition, the [family] have turned to you for help.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Heroic Stand

options.text: With a public funeral and games.
Publicly swear to avenge him.
He did a soldier’s duty, that is all.

events.text: Forced to retreat, [character] and a handful of volunteers from amongst his troops held off the pursuing [rival] forces for three days and three nights while the tattered remainder of his army escaped. The tale of their sacrifice has swept [city] with fervor, and some of the returning troops have rallied the people in a militia of those inspired by [character]. How will you honor the fallen heroes?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Honored Enemy

options.text: We should all follow [character]’s example.
[character] was weak.

events.text: The somber procession arrives at your court. The cold body of [character] is accompanied by a message from your enemy [character], surprisingly humble in tone. “Although he was our enemy, [character] was a reputable foe and always treated us with respect. We return the body, so that you may honor him.”

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Into the Mist

options.text: Encourage the hero myth.
Have his deeds written down in an epic.
Praise his family, the [family].

events.text: Most of the bodies have already been stripped clean of their valuables by the time your soldiers are able to return to the field of battle to retrieve the bodies of the fallen. But amongst the living or the dead, there is no sign of [character]. One soldier accounts that they last saw him walking into a sudden mist that arose during the fighting. True or not, stories are soon spreading through your armies of the hero [character], who will one day return to defend [rival].

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Killed in Action

options.text: A private gathering for friends and family.
Parades through the streets of the capital.
Days of rest for the military.

events.text: A rider in black brings a message from the front lines: your son [character], a soldier, has died in the line of duty. It is said that he served with distinction. How do you wish to honor your fallen hero?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Like a [title]

options.text: A city is a small price for your life.
Die as you lived, as a [title].

events.text: Even defeated and bleeding, you remain standing, dignified and unyielding. Surrounded and fighting to the last, eventually you are taken by the triumphant [rival] forces and brought before [character]. The [title] demands that you cede [city] to [rival].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Lover Lost

options.text: I will embrace my grief.
I must remain strong for my people.

events.text: You know the news before the messenger tells you. An emptiness in your heart whispers that your lover, [character], has been slain in battle. The messenger’s words sound distant and you barely register when he leaves the room. Your lover is gone, all you can do is decide how to respond to this cruel act of fate.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Needless Bloodshed

options.text: We will continue our current strategy.
Order troops in the field to stand down.
Send a veteran officer to improve training.

events.text: The recent combat losses are the talk of the capital. Bloodshed always causes an outpouring of sorrow. [character] implores you to reconsider any further deployment of troops. He worries that the court may be acting recklessly with the lives of its soldiers. What shall we do?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Restless General

options.text: Take time to rest and read.
Encourage [character] to return to duty as soon as possible.

events.text: When you talk to [character], there is no sign that there is anything wrong. But, whenever he thinks that you aren’t looking, there is a grimace of pain and his weight shifts away from his left leg where you know a vicious wound lies under his armor. In the recent fighting, [character] was struck in the leg with an arrow. The barbs ripped through his flesh, but missed the longer-lasting damage of striking bone. Even so, it is a feat of impressive will that [character] is up on his feet, let alone asking to be let back onto the battlefield as soon as possible.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Stories of Glory

options.text: Our national stories should be celebrated.
The outside world holds [rival]'s future.
Regale [character] with tales of foreign lands.

events.text: Following our recent victories, some members of the court have begun to question our commitment to foreign exploration. A faction led by [character] and the [family] family believes that our laws should be changed to celebrate personal glory and national might. How shall we respond?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Sudden Savior

options.text: Reward them with a position in your court.
Thank the troops with paid leave.

events.text: The battlefield is in chaos and you are in the center of the fray. Your shield is in tatters, hacked apart by the heavy blows of your enemy. Finally the shield can bear no longer and a heavily swung axe breaks through and bites into your arm. The adrenaline and the pain fight to hold you in their grip. Before you can sink to the floor, rough hands grab the back of your armor, pulling you away from the fray. You later discover that upon seeing you surrounded, an officer rallied the men and led a sortie to save you. Will you reward this sudden savior?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Fallen Banner

options.text: Berate [character] for allowing the banner to fall.
Encourage [character] that he will have a chance to redeem himself.

events.text: After the fighting is done, the few survivors under [character] slink back to the capital. They bring reports that their banner was lost in the battle, despite [character] surviving. [character], strict even for a general, demands that [character] should be publicly denounced for letting the banner fall, but the defeated leader was carried from the battle after an early arrow pierced his armor.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Furies

options.text: Pursue those that would wrong us!
No, such titles will distract from their training.

events.text: Upon hearing of the fall of [character] forces, one of your [unit] units comes forward, swearing to avenge the loss. They ask to be renamed to "The Furies" after the Greek goddesses of vengeance, promising to not rest until the [rival] forces are defeated.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Trapped General

options.text: We move immediately.
[character] is lost.

events.text: A soldier rushes into your presence, carrying news from [character]. The general has fallen back after the recent loss, retreating with his remaining soldiers to a nearby ruin. However, after the [rival] army advanced they are now trapped and unable to move, surrounded by enemy forces. It is only a matter of time before they are found and killed. A small team of local guides and select soldiers may be able to get him back to safety, but doing so would be no easy feat. Shall we send help for [character]?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: War Blunders

options.text: Throw a private feast in honor of myself.
I will buy their loyalty with gold.

events.text: After your recent mistakes in battle, some of the other officers doubt your prowess. They worry that your ego far outweighs your ability. How will you react?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Wounded General

options.text: Let him rest.
Pay for the finest medics.
Ask for divine intervention.
Put your best knowledge to use.

events.text: [character] is brought back to you wounded and barely breathing, his body covered in brutal wounds from the fighting. The chances of recovery are slim, but will you intervene to attempt to save [character]’s life?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: [character] Wounded

options.text: Hopefully he shall return to the fight soon.

events.text: A messenger arrives with news of [character]’s defeat. Despite the loss of his forces, [character] managed to escape, although he was wounded in the fighting.
